fact: The OGP page for commitment LR0036, citing the IRM report on interviews and a site visit in October 2018, says the national data portal (eLiberia) was live but not formally launched, with links to ministry and agency sites and an unpopulated data repository page; the document ties it to no open data policy.

The EITI validation report says LEITI's online Data Portal has significantly improved the openness of extractive data, and that the LEITI Data Warehouse provides production and export data disaggregated by company; no dataset count or licence is stated. The date is the report's own (2026-07-23), as it describes the portal at work.

fact: The LISGIS microdata catalogue lists the anonymised Liberia Annual Agricultural Survey 2024 household dataset as a Public Use File accessible to all for statistical and research purposes, released as version 1.0 (record last modified 1 July 2026); redistribution needs LISGIS written agreement, so no open licence is stated.

The LISGIS final report says the LAAS-2024 final report is available online on the LISGIS site and the survey microdata can be obtained from the LISGIS microdata catalogue; document dated October 2025.

LISGIS notice LISGIS/DG/ODL/2026/001, effective 8 June 2026, names CC BY 4.0 as its licence standard and grants a worldwide royalty-free licence to use and redistribute its data, including data on its open data portal, commercially and non-commercially with attribution.

ODI Global says the Liberia Development Dashboard, run by the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning on government servers, has all its data publicly available and downloadable in various formats, with no licence stated.

Liberia's Public Procurement and Concessions Commission publishes open contracting data from its e-procurement system, downloadable in JSON, Excel or CSV, per the Open Contracting Partnership registry; no licence is stated in the page text.
